This appeal has been filed under Section 23 of the Railways Claims Tribunal Act 1987 being aggrieved by the judgment dated 11.8.2017 passed in Claim Application No. O.A.
IIU/BPL/2013/00391 in the matter of Anandram Kol and others Vs. Union of India.

sentences.text: Learned Claims tribunal, Bhopal Bench, district Bhopal dismissed the application filed by the claimant for compensation.

2. The facts of the are that on 7.3.2013 the deceased Vinod Kumar Kol died in the Railway accident due to fall from the running train when he was travelling from Pendra Road to Tenganmadra by Train No. 18204.
After the accident, the deceased was taken to hospital for treatment but he expired.

In untoward accident, the claimants/ appellants, who are parents of the deceased filed an application for compensation under Section 16 of the RCT Act seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.4 lacs for the death of their unmarried son.
The deceased - Vinod Kumar Kol fell down from the running train due to jerk.

He was admitted in SIMS hospital and died.
3.

The respondent replied that the deceased was travelling in wrong 2 MA-3020-2017 train after purchasing second class journey ticket, which was not valid for the concerned train and since he boarded a wrong train and since the train did not have a scheduled halt at the destination where the deceased wanted to go, therefore, after knowing this fact, he tried to get down from the moving train, therefore, the cause of accident is his own mistake and railway is not liable to pay any compensation.
4. The appeal has been filed by the appellants on the ground that it is wrong to say that the deceased was not a bona fide passenger.
By D.R.M. report, it is established that deceased was travelling in the wrong train.
It was not a valid ticket for the said train by which the deceased was travelling.

6. Perused the record.
The question before this bench is whether in the facts and circumstances of the case the dismissal of the claim application was correct or not.

Learned Claims Tribunal in its judgment dated 11.8.2017 has held that the applicant has filed certified copies of Ex. A-1 to A-10,
affidavit of applicant's witness - Anand Ram Kol, who has been examined.
The respondent-Railway has filed R-1 DRM report.
It has been held that no pleading about loss of ticket or seizure of the said ticket was taken by the Police after the said accident.
There is no proof of purchasing of valid ticket.

It has been mentioned in Para -1 by learned Claims Tribunal that as per statement of co- passenger given to I.O. of G.R.P., Dongargarh, they have stated that in DRM report that the deceased had purchased ticket for the journey from Pendra Road to Tenganmada.
It was stated by Sonu Kol that the Police seized ticket but it has not made available on record either the by the applicant or by the respondent.
Therefore, it was held that the deceased did not have any ticket.
The witnesses of Panchanama are friends of the deceased who have stated that he was travelling from Pendra Road Tenganmada to Bilaspur, which is not proved.

Though attempt has been made to rectify the contention of the applicant in claim petition as train no.
3 MA-3020-2017 12804 does not have a scheduled halt at Tenganmada Station and the deceased was travelling from Pendra Road to Bilaspur by Train No. 18204 on a second class ticket which was not valid.
It was stated that the deceased boarded the wrong train, i.e. Train No.18204, Betwa Express, which was an Express Train and did not have stop at Tenganmade Station.

The applicant has also stated that his son attempted to get down from the train for the same reason at Belghana Station when the train was in slow motion on loop line, he lost his balance and met with an accident.
7. It is also mentioned that the applicant Anandram Kol in cross examination admitted that he had informed the I.O., RPF that he did not have any knowledge where his son had gone.
He came to know about the accident later on.
It has been held that the accident occurred due to dare devil act of the deceased and this fault would not come within the ambit of an accidental fall.
Therefore, the accident would come under the exceptional Clauses (a) to (e) of Section 124-A of the Railway Act.
It has been held that under Section 124 of Railways act there is no provision to provide the compensation to an injured or in case of death suffered by passenger regardless of the causative factors.

8. The deceased tried to get down from the train.

sentences.text:
We are of the considered view that the High Court gravely erred in holding that the applicants were not entitled to any compensation under Section 124-A of the Act,
because the deceased had died by falling down from the train because of his own negligence.
First, the case of the Railways that the deceased M. Hafeez was standing at the open door of the train compartment in a negligent manner from where he fell down is entirely based on speculation.

There is admittedly no eyewitness to the fall of the deceased from the train and, therefore, there is absolutely no evidence to support the case of the Railways that the accident took place in the manner suggested by it.

Secondly, even if it were to be assumed that the deceased fell from the train to his death due to his own negligence it will not have any effect on the compensation payable under Section 124-A of the Act.

9 .The manner in which the accident is sought to be reconstructed by the Railways,
that the deceased was standing at the open door of the train compartment from where he fell down, is called by the Railways itself as negligence.
Now negligence of this kind which is not very uncommon on Indian trains is not the same thing as a criminal act mentioned in clause (c) to the proviso to Section 124-A.
A criminal act envisaged under clause ( c) must have an element of malicious intent or mens rea.
Standing at the open doors of the compartment of a running train may be a negligent act, even a rash act but, without anything else, it is certainly not a criminal act.

Thus,
the case of the Railways must fail even after assuming everything in its favour.
10. We are, therefore, constrained to interfere in the matter.
The judgment and order of the High Court coming under appeal is set aside and the judgment and order of the Tribunal is restored.

Since a period of more than 10 years has already elapsed from the date of the judgment of the Tribunal, the compensation money along with interest need not be kept in fixed deposits, but should be paid to the appellants in the ratio fixed by the Tribunal.
The payment must be made within 2 months from today."

sentences.text: Explanation: For the purposes of this section, "passenger" includes- (i) a railway servant on duty; and (ii) a person who has purchased a valid ticket for travelling, by a train carrying passengers, on any date or a valid platform ticket and becomes a victim of an untoward incident'
For claiming compensation under Section 124-A, it is not necessary to show that there is any negligence on the part of the railway administration.
It is also not necessary to establish that the injured was not negligent.
The negligence of either the Railway administration or that of the injured is not relevant under Section 124-A.
The negligence of the claimant cannot disentitle him from claiming compensation under Section 124-A.
Admittedly, the accident occurred not as a part of an attempt of suicide.
It is not a self inflicted injury or he has not done any criminal act.
Mere negligence on the part of the bonafide passenger is not a ground to deny the compensation for untoward incident.
Like Section 163 A of the Motor Vehicles Act, strict 6 MA-3020-2017 liability is cast on the railway administration for payment of compensation.
In the explanation to the Section, it is stated that even if a person has a platform ticket and became a victim of untoward incident, he will come within the Section.

If there is an untoward incident in the course of working in a railway and if a passenger is injured or killed in such incident, the injured or the dependents of the passenger will be entitled to get compensation from Railway administration unless the passenger dies or suffers injury due to any of the reasons stated in (a) to (e) of the proviso t o Section 124-A.

4 passenger in this case does not come under (a) to (e) of proviso to Section 124-A the claim cannot be rejected.

sentences.text:
3. The 'untoward incident' is defined under Section 123 (c) which reads as follows:
"(c) 'untoward incident' means- (1) (i) the commission of a terrorist act within the meaning of Sub-section (1) of Section 3 of the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987; or (ii) the making of a violent attack or the commission of robbery or dacoity; or (iii) the indulging in rioting, shoot-out or arson, by any person in or on any train carrying passengers, or in a waiting hall, cloak room or reservation or booking office or on any platform or in any other place within the precincts of a railway station; or (2) the accidental falling of any passenger from a train carrying passengers'."
Certainly the injury was caused as a result of the untoward incident.
It is not an intended injury.
In the above circumstances, the railway administration is liable to pay compensation.
10. Thus, it is clear that while getting down from the train and falling accidentally when the passenger boarded a wrong train, there is no disentitledment of parents from the compensation.
Accordingly, in the facts and circumstances of the case and the case of Thomas (supra) it is found that learned tribunal has not taken a correct view in the case at hand.
11. Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case recovery of ticket is of no consequence.
Hence, appellants/claimants are entitled for the reliefs claimed.
Accordingly, judgment of the Tribunal is set aside.

As the accident 7 MA-3020-2017 is of 11.08.2017 therefore, the appellants would be entitled for compensation of Rs.4 lacs alongwith interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of accident till the payment.
12. In the result, the appeal is disposed of accordingly.
